# R4 — Tested at Kadesh-Barnea: Avoid the Congregation of the Disobedient (3:1–4:13)

**Range read in full:** slice lines 2117–2383 (source body for Heb 3:1–4:13)  
**Source:** Cockerill, *The Epistle to the Hebrews* (NICNT, 2012)  
**Evidence class default:** Cockerill (commentary exposition; “the pastor” = author of Hebrews as Cockerill frames him).  
**Section heading in source:** B. Tested at Kadesh-Barnea: Avoid the Congregation of the Disobedient (3:1–4:13)

## Claims

### C1 — Section role: second half of “Very Short History of the Disobedient”
**Locus:** 2119  
**Quote:** "Heb 3:1-4:13 is the second half of \"A Very Short History of the Disobedient\" people of God that brings the story of their rebellion to its conclusion."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) After Sinai continuity (1:1–2:18), the pastor associates addressees who received God’s word in Christ with the wilderness generation; comparison of Son with Moses (3:1–6) via Num 12:7–8 leads naturally to applying Kadesh-Barnea (Num 13–14) through the ready-made exhortation of Ps 95:7b–11 (warning 3:7–19; enter forfeited rest 4:1–11), ending with accountability before the penetrating word (4:12–13) that reinforces 1:1–3.

### C2 — Continuity of one house; Moses steward / Christ Son; delayed explanation of faithfulness
**Locus:** 2121  
**Quote:** "the Son and Moses both function in the one house of God composed of the wilderness generation led by Moses as well as those who have received God's word in his Son… Moses functions as a \"steward\" but Christ as a \"Son\" prepares for the typological relationship between the old and new orders of salvation in 4:14-10:18."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Heb 3:1–6 grounds OT examples as negative (3:7–4:11) and positive (11:1–40); Son’s faithfulness is affirmed but delayed in explanation until 4:14–10:18 (esp. 5:7–10; 10:5–10) as turning point between faithless and faithful; Jesus (12:1–3) becomes supreme example and empowerer of perseverance.  
**Pages:** `hebrews`, `moses`, `gareth-lee-cockerill`

### C3 — Wilderness generation example, not “type”; same rest, same faith/obedience
**Locus:** 2123  
**Quote:** "That generation is an example for but not a \"type\" of Christian believers. Both groups are part of the one people of God called by his word to the same kind of faith and obedience in anticipation of the same \"rest.\""  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Continuity is maximized by delaying superior Christian privileges; loss of rest is sternest warning; hearers urged to separate from predecessors by persevering obedience—not typological supercession that severs identity.

### C4 — Kadesh climax, not forty-year wandering as pilgrimage model (vs Käsemann)
**Locus:** 2125  
**Quote:** "Käsemann has argued that the pastor is drawing an analogy between his hearers and the forty years of wilderness wandering. However, Hofius, Vanhoye, and Laansma have shown that wilderness wandering is not the theme of this passage… the forty years of wilderness wandering was not a model for this pilgrimage but the fate of those who proved faithless at pilgrimage's end."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill, following Hofius/Vanhoye/Laansma; Benetreau adjustment) Focus is Kadesh-Barnea (Num 14) as climax of disobedience since Sinai/Egypt; Greek Ps 95 suppresses other wilderness events; Heb 11 may describe pilgrimage to the City, but 3:7–4:11 places the people at what should have been pilgrimage’s end.  
**Pages:** `hebrews`, `promised-land`, `gareth-lee-cockerill`

### C5 — No single impending “Kadesh event”; drift → irreversible unbelief
**Locus:** 2127  
**Quote:** "the pastor is not concerned merely about a specific crisis his hearers may face but about their perseverance until the end… If left unchecked, the unbelief incipient in such behavior leads to the kind of irreversible disobedience and ultimate loss experienced by their ancestors at Kadesh."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Rejects Lane’s persecution-as-Kadesh alone and Hofius’s “final revelation as ultimate decision” as insufficient; Kadesh combines crowning disobedience with final judgment; awakens them re 2:1–4 neglect/drift; final “Kadesh” is entrance/exclusion at the Unshakable Kingdom (12:25–29).  
**Pages:** `hebrews-warning-passages`

### C6 — 3:1: Consider Jesus, Apostle and High Priest of our confession
**Locus:** 2131–2133, 2139  
**Quote:** "consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession, Jesus… \"Apostle\" encapsulates what the pastor has said in 1:1-2:4 about the Son as God's final and complete revelation… \"High Priest\" portrays him as the one who has provided \"such a great salvation.\""  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Urgent invitation sets sermon direction through 12:1–3; “Apostle” (rare for Christ before Justin) summarizes final revelation and superiority to prophets, angels, Moses; “High Priest” anticipates Aaron comparison; grammatical bond = revelation fulfilled through high-priestly sacrifice; name “Jesus” reserved for emphatic end.  
**Pages:** `hebrews`, `moses`

### C7 — Holy brothers, partakers of heavenly calling
**Locus:** 2137  
**Quote:** "\"Holy brothers and sisters\" reminds them of who they are as the people of God… \"partakers in the heavenly calling.\"… This \"calling\" is an invitation to heaven and from heaven… ultimate destination is the \"heavenly homeland\" (11:16)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Address grounds identity in Son who makes holy (2:11–12); calling invites present access to Most Holy Place for perseverance-grace and ultimate City/homeland/Jerusalem; partakers via partaking in the seated Son (3:14; 1:13).

### C8 — Faithfulness of Jesus: earthly and exalted continuous
**Locus:** 2145  
**Quote:** "This faithfulness includes both the incarnate obedience of \"Jesus\" and the resultant continuing trustworthiness of the exalted \"Apostle and High Priest\"… The deliberate use of the present participle, being faithful, encompasses both past earthly and present heavenly faithfulness in one continuous reality."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Adverbial “as being faithful” (not mere relative clause); anticipates 10:7 “to do your will”; contrasts wilderness unfaithfulness; salvation initiated by God who appointed him, accomplished in incarnate obedience, mediated by exalted High Priest.

### C9 — House = God’s people; Moses via Num 12, not Philo/heavenly-mediator speculation
**Locus:** 2151  
**Quote:** "This \"house\" is God's people once led by Moses and now brought to glory by the Son… The pastor makes no use of Jewish speculations about Moses as a heavenly mediator. Nor does he follow Philo… His comments are based on the OT in general and on Numbers 12 in particular."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Formal comparison on shared faithfulness; Moses chosen as premier OT revelation-agent, Old Covenant mediator, leader who established foreshadowing priesthood—not because ranked above angels after 1:5–14.  
**Pages:** `moses`, `hebrews`

### C10 — Greater glory: builder vs house; establish = complete/equip people of God
**Locus:** 2153–2155  
**Quote:** "He is due greater \"glory\" than Moses in proportion to the greater \"honor\" due the builder of a \"house\" than the \"house\" itself… As the fulfillment of revelation and the provider of redemption the Son brings God's people to their inheritance and intended end… He is due greater \"glory\" because he surpasses Moses as the Redeemer surpasses the redeemed."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) “This one” (not inserted “Jesus”) broadens to reserve “Son” for v. 6; glory suited to revelation of God’s glory (1:3; 2:10) beyond Moses’ limited vision (Exod 33); “establish” can mean build or furnish/equip (cf. 9:2, 6); pre- and post-incarnation people reach goal through him (11:39–40)—not preincarnate-builder speculation.

### C11 — v. 4: Son as “all-things establishing one” / Creator
**Locus:** 2157–2159  
**Quote:** "the second affirms the deity of the Son as Creator… it is no surprise when he calls the Son \"the all-things establishing one\" and reaffirms his deity… Failure to accept this verse as confirmation of the Son's divine creatorship leaves it a foreign body in the text."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Transition from household-of-people to household-of-creation; “establish” spans Creator and heir who brings all to end through redemption; deity affirmation introduces Son over house where Moses is steward.

### C12 — Moses steward (θεράπων) vs Christ Son over house; witness of things yet spoken
**Locus:** 2161–2167  
**Quote:** "Moses was faithful in all his house as a steward… Christ as a Son over his house… His stewardship consists in being a \"witness of things yet to be spoken.\"… By establishing the sacrificial system Moses bore witness to the atoning sacrifice and high priesthood of Christ."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Chiastic contrast; no denigration of Moses—unparalleled OT channel (Num 12); only Moses regularly “steward of God” from Genesis to Joshua end; Son Creator-Redeemer is over, not highest servant in, the house; Mosaic system’s salvific ineffectiveness does not cancel its witness function.  
**Pages:** `moses`, `hebrews`

### C13 — “Whose house we are if we hold fast”: one people including OT faithful
**Locus:** 2169–2171  
**Quote:** "Since Moses himself was a \"steward\" in God's house, there is no reason to limit this household to a supposed \"new\" people of God… those who lived before Christ also enter God's heavenly homeland only through him."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Privilege + perseverance contingency; wilderness generation and ch. 11 faithful are potent examples because one people; v. 14 restates same truth more Christologically.

### C14 — Against Fanning: condition not mere evidence of inevitable perseverance of true believers
**Locus:** 2173–2177  
**Quote:** "While such use of the conditional is possible, the implications that Fanning would draw fit neither the larger nor the immediate context… the pastor never suggests that the full adequacy of Christ as Savior guarantees the perseverance of true believers… These are the people that the pastor urges in equally strong terms to persevere lest they suffer ultimate loss."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Fanning’s inferential-conditional (future perseverance evidences present reality as house) fails: Christ provides means and compelling reason to persevere, not automatic guarantee; pastor addresses hearers as true believers (“holy… partakers… house… participants in Christ… enlightened… Holy Spirit… powers of the age to come”); Guthrie’s “pastoral ignorance” refuge also rejected; Fanning’s view makes wilderness generation never truly God’s people despite Moses stewarding them.  
**Pages:** `hebrews-warning-passages`, `gareth-lee-cockerill`

### C15 — Hold fast boldness and boasting in hope: present access + future reward
**Locus:** 2183  
**Quote:** "through the work of Christ believers have been given \"boldness\" for present entrance into God's presence… This \"boldness\" is not a mere feeling but the right or privilege of access to God… they are to maintain their \"boasting\" in the \"hope\" of that future which will be theirs through Christ at his return."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Present privileges motivate contingent holding-fast; boldness = high-priestly access enabling public profession; boasting in hope = robust faith in future reward vs temporal rewards; wilderness example clarifies failure to hold fast.

### C16 — Structure of 3:7–19: quote → today/heart/harden → rebellion consequences
**Locus:** 2193–2195  
**Quote:** "instead of beginning with Num 13:1-14:45, the pastor expounds the ready-made exhortation in this psalm, first as a warning against imitating the wilderness generation (Heb 3:7-19), then as encouragement to enter the blessing that generation forfeited (4:1-11)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Three subsections: Ps 95:7–11 quote (vv. 7–11); application on today/heart/harden (12–14; expands 3:6); rebellion magnitude/consequences (15–19); bookend “see” (12) and what they “see” (19).

### C17 — Holy Spirit still says; hearing as choice and obedience
**Locus:** 2197  
**Quote:** "\"As the Holy Spirit\" even now \"says\" marks this psalm as the direct and unavoidable address of God to the hearers in the present… \"If you will hear his voice\" is an appeal not to imitate the wilderness generation."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) “Therefore” links 3:6 hold-fast to “do not harden”; hearing is occasion for choice and, in Greek contingent sense, synonymous with obedience.

### C18 — LXX Meribah/Massah as rebellion/testing; focus still Kadesh
**Locus:** 2199–2207  
**Quote:** "Hebrews, following the LXX, retains the meaning of these terms by translating them as \"rebellion\" and \"testing,\" but loses their local significance… Yet even in Hebrew the focus of this psalm was not on the event recorded in Exod 17:1-7, but on the refusal… at Kadesh-Barnea… Their refusal to trust God's power and promise at Kadesh was the fatal climax of a history of disobedience."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) English “Meribah/Massah” place-names lose meaning; LXX descriptive translation strengthens warning and lets Ps 95:11 Kadesh rest-oath dominate; Exod 17 sets direction climaxing at Kadesh; “rebellion” first (reversed order) stresses gravity; fits Num 14:35 “wicked congregation.”  
**Pages:** `promised-land`, `hebrews`

### C19 — “Therefore” and forty years: interpretive arrangement of Ps 95:9–10
**Locus:** 2209–2223  
**Quote:** "Verse 17 below suggests that the pastor knew and interpreted this psalm in its standard form without the \"therefore.\"… It is very possible, then, that he has purposefully inserted this \"therefore\" with the intention of stressing the causal connection between the people's \"testing\" God… and the divine anger… It is more probable that the pastor identified God's \"works\" not only with his acts of wilderness sustenance but also, perhaps even predominantly, with God's acts of judgment."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Hebrews’ added “therefore” (not in known LXX witnesses) rearranges: forty years qualifies “saw my works” rather than “I was angry”; pastor’s v. 17 still knows standard form; purpose = inevitable link disobedience→displeasure; “works for forty years” likely includes judgment works, not a pre-Kadesh blessing period only.

### C20 — Divine oath frames exclusion, rest availability, and later guarantees
**Locus:** 2225  
**Quote:** "the pastor will use this oath both as the conclusion of his warning (3:17) and as the basis, in 4:1-11 (v. 3), of his assurance that \"there remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God\" (4:9)… counterpart in God's oath to Abraham (6:13-20)… fulfilled because it rests on God's oath to his Son in Ps 110:4."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Faithless fate, Christ’s sufficiency, and faithful destiny all guaranteed by divine oath; living by faith = living in accord with this reality.  
**Pages:** `sabbath`, `hebrews-warning-passages`

### C21 — Evil heart of unbelief; fall away from the living God
**Locus:** 2229–2241  
**Quote:** "\"Unbelief\" is the most comprehensive description of the sin of the wilderness generation… encompasses disobedience, for it is both the refusal (or willing failure) to trust God and the consequent lack of faithfulness to God… \"to fall away from the living God\"… By their refusal they were acting as if he were not \"living.\""  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Present vigilance lest any have evil unbelieving heart; ten spies’ unbelief destroyed many; opposite = true heart / full assurance of faith (10:22) with laws written on heart; unbelief climaxed at Kadesh denying power and imminent rest-promise; “living God” = God who acts and keeps word; exclusion proves he is living; not primarily idolatry temptation—faithless living equals idolaters’ loss; abandoning Christ = abandoning whole work of God (even if return to pre-Christian Jewish security).  
**Pages:** `hebrews-warning-passages`, `promised-land`

### C22 — Rest lost = City/homeland of ch. 11 faithful
**Locus:** 2235  
**Quote:** "the \"rest\" lost by the wilderness generation is to be identified with the eternal \"City\" (11:10-11; 12:22; 13:14) and heavenly \"homeland\" (11:13-16) anticipated by the OT faithful… both \"rest\" and \"Promised Land\" referred to the same reality in the OT."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Parallel unbelief vs “by faith” deeds coordinates pastoral strategy; OT rest/land identity undergirds eternal reading of forfeited rest.  
**Pages:** `promised-land`, `sabbath`, `hebrews`

### C23 — Mutual daily exhortation “while it is called today”; sin’s deceit
**Locus:** 2245–2251  
**Quote:** "\"exhort one another daily while it is called `today.\"'… mutual exhortation… must encompass both encouragement to embrace the promises of God and warning… \"Sin,\" singular, is a besetting… power that deceives by causing people to see only the things of this world and not the invisible-to-the-human-eye possibilities of God."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Antidote to evil heart: regular intentional mutual care (opposite of ten spies); “today” may close via hardened refusal (6:4–8) though for obedient lasts to Judgment/death; hardening by repeated failure; sin blinded them to Canaanite power vs God’s greatness (Num 14); passive of permission—“do not allow yourselves to be hardened”; “Instead of allowing sin to make them resistant to the word of God, the listeners are to allow the word of God to make them resistant to [sin].”

### C24 — Participants in Christ if hold beginning of steadfastness firm to the end
**Locus:** 2253–2259  
**Quote:** "to be… part of this \"house\" over which Christ presides as Son is to be \"participants\" in Christ… Continuing participation in Christ is dependent upon… \"if only we hold the beginning of our steadfastness firm until the end.\"… little support for the subjective reading \"confidence\" or \"assurance\"… Reference to the initial steadfastness evidenced… after their conversion as described in 10:32-35."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Perfect “we have become” = conversion-entry into continuing share; more intimate than house-image; not equal “partners”—benefits all from Christ; possible NAB-like “beginning of the reality” (cf. 1:3 hypostasis of God); steadfastness = dependable resolve/conduct and bold witness (3:6), not mere subjective attitude; hold firm because saving revelation is utterly [dependable].  
**Pages:** `hebrews-warning-passages`

### C25 — 3:16–19 interrogation: rebellion, sin, disobedience → unbelief; not “some but not all”
**Locus:** 2263–2271, 2281  
**Quote:** "This rebellion is described as \"sin\" \"disobedience\" (v. 18), and finally as \"unbelief\" (v. 19)… \"For who, although they had heard, rebelled? Was it not all those who came out of Egypt through Moses?\"… Many early interpreters… \"some… but not all\"… the context lends strong support to the interrogative interpretation."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Rhetorical questions escalate to 3:19 peak anticipating 6:1–8 and 10:26–31; aorist “rebelled” = Kadesh event; concessive “although they had heard” = culpability; rejects early “some/not all” (Moses, Aaron, Caleb, Joshua exemption) as unnecessary and contextually weak; unbelief = ultimate comprehensive descriptor including direct climactic refusal.

### C26 — Forty years wrath; corpses in desert; oath excludes from rest
**Locus:** 2275–2279  
**Quote:** "his wrath was unrelenting until the death of the last rebel… \"Fallen corpses\" describes a death appropriate for apostates… The oath of God established with absolute certainty the irreversible exclusion of those who \"disobeyed\" at Kadesh from God's \"rest\"… The God who pronounces unremitting judgment on the faithless promises unfailing grace to the faithful."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Sustained yet wrath-marked wandering until death; desert death vs rest blessing; prepares apostasy warnings; mention of rest anticipates 4:1–11 hope; certainty of oath also undergirds provision for entrance (6:13–20; Ps 110:4 Guarantor).

### C27 — Not mere temporal Canaan loss; rest = God’s eternal rest for modern believers
**Locus:** 2283  
**Quote:** "Some have argued that since the OT is referring only to the loss of physical Canaan the author of Hebrews is threatening the hearers with mere temporal punishment… By omitting the word \"rest\" in 3:19 the pastor invites his hearers to ask what it was… He answers… the \"rest\" forfeited… was God's eternal \"rest\" promised to modern believers."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Rejects temporal-only reading as introducing OT-absent temporal/eternal split; encourages faithfulness and appetite for high-priestly teaching as provision for perseverance and final entrance.  
**Pages:** `promised-land`, `sabbath`, `hebrews-warning-passages`

### C28 — 4:1–11 frame: fear / diligence; redirect from unbelief to rest still open
**Locus:** 2289–2295  
**Quote:** "framed in vv. 1 and 11 by renewed warnings… Yet the pastor would redirect his hearers' primary attention from the unbelief of the wilderness generation to the \"rest\" they forfeited… he must establish both its nature and its continued availability."

### C29 — Two image-fields: Promised Land (final) vs Most Holy Place (present access)
**Locus:** 2299  
**Quote:** "When he is urging them to persevere until final entrance at the return of Christ, he uses Promised Land language… \"rest\"… \"homeland\"… \"City\"… When he encourages them to draw near in the present… he speaks of the Most Holy Place… although the pastor uses the imagery… in different ways, he is aware that they describe the same reality… grand climactic picture in 12:22-24."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Structural key for OT use and sermon shape; OT anticipators of Land fit final perseverance; Tent ritual fits daily approach; convergence at City = Most Holy Place (cf. Rev 21).

### C30 — Laansma/Hofius: rest is local and future (place, not mere state)
**Locus:** 2301  
**Quote:** "Laansma, following Hofius, has demonstrated conclusively that the \"rest\" of chapters 3 and 4 is both local and future… Few books in the NT assert more emphatically the concrete nature of the ultimate destiny of God's people than does Hebrews… nothing in 3:1-4:13 that suggests present entrance besides the present tense verb of 4:3… progressive or futuristic, \"we are in the process of entering into rest\"… The attempt to introduce this idea in these chapters only begets confusion."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Rest = place of joining God penultimately at death, finally at Judgment; identity with homeland/City; enter-able; LXX and Second Temple usage confirm local; Promised Land imagery unsuitable for present-entrance descriptions because it equates contemporary believers with OT anticipators; present high-priestly access is real but *not* what 3–4 discuss—anti-abstract/state (and thus anti-Platonic-mystical present-rest) reading of this pericope.  
**Pages:** `sabbath`, `promised-land`, `hebrews-worldview-platonic-vs-apocalyptic`, `gareth-lee-cockerill`

### C31 — 4:1: Let us fear; promise of entering still remains; fallen short at Judgment
**Locus:** 2303–2309  
**Quote:** "\"let us fear lest\"… \"because a promise of entering his rest still remains\"… fear lest \"any of you be found to have fallen short.\"… not… \"seem to have fallen\"… come short of their eternal goal at the Judgment."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Stronger than 3:12 “see”; author includes self; promise is of *entering* not bare rest; temporal force while promise remains—can forfeit; same promise as Abraham’s homeland, oath-guaranteed (6:13–20), certified by Jesus’ entrance (6:19–20); faith = life on certainty of promise and power; perfect “have fallen short” echoes permanent Kadesh exclusion and anticipates apostasy texts.

### C34 — Ps 95:11 + Gen 2:2: God’s rest since creation; tension and resolution
**Locus:** 2321–2329

### C41 — 4:12–13 closes first major section: living word, accountability, wordplay
**Locus:** 2365–2381  
**Quote:** "This first large section of Hebrews (1:1-4:13), which began with God's final revelation in his Son (1:1-4), ends with a compelling assertion of human accountability before the word of God… Like God himself… his word is \"living\" and thus \"active\"… \"sharper than any two-edged sword\"… \"discerning or judging the thoughts and intentions of the heart\"… \"naked and prostrate\" before his eyes… \"to whom a word of reckoning is due from us.\""  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Great salvation/rest promise entails judgment for rejecters; also closes 3:1–4:11 wilderness story; “living” word = creative (11:3), prophetic then Son-spoken, still addressing via sermon (Ps 95); cannot evade; divides indivisible (life/spirit, joints/marrow)—Smillie surgeon’s-knife feel not developed lest soften warning; exposes heart by confronting with God’s claims (as at Kadesh); call to repentance of lethargy/unbelief; God already knows—nothing created hidden; “laid bare” (throat-related) = helpless prostration (Montefiore); ends with answering “word” of reckoning; trepidation prepares 4:14–16 High Priest reassurance.  
**Pages:** `hebrews`, `hebrews-warning-passages`

### C42 — First warning chain paired with 10:26–31
**Locus:** 2369  
**Quote:** "It is important to compare this warning that concludes the opening section of Hebrews, with 10:26-31… Both warnings stress accountability. The first ends… \"word of reckoning\"… the second with, \"It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God\" (10:31). The first derives its urgency from the magnitude of the promised \"rest\"; the second adds greater urgency from the full adequacy of Christ's saving work."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) 4:12–13 prepares reception of high-priestly benefits (4:14–16) to avoid wilderness faithlessness; 10:26–31, after 5:1–10:18 benefits, motivates identification with faithful (11:1–38)—two poles of first major warning architecture.  
**Pages:** `hebrews-warning-passages`, `hebrews`

### C43 — Confession: act and content; possible formal confession; high-priestly teaching new
**Locus:** 2143  
**Quote:** "It is virtually impossible to separate the act of confessing from the truth confessed… even if the pastor did not introduce the high-priestly title to this congregation, his teaching on this subject was certainly new… required Scriptural justification (7:1-28) and was difficult… (5:11-14)."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) “Apostle and High Priest of our confession” may reflect community worship confession; “Son” widely familiar; high priesthood used to explain significance of affirmations (4:14–16; 10:19–25).

### C44 — Section 3:1–4:13 pastoral purpose summary (first major warning complex)
**Locus:** 2119–2127, 2285–2289, 2361–2369  
**Quote:** "This carefully constructed section plays an essential role in the pastor's overall purpose of motivating his hearers to faithful endurance… Avoid the Company of the Faithless Generation… Pursue the Blessing Lost by the Faithless Generation… You Are Accountable before the Word of God."  
**Claim:** (Cockerill) Unit is first major warning chain: (1) fix eyes on faithful Son over house; (2) do not harden like Kadesh rebels; (3) fear and strive to enter still-open Sabbath rest; (4) face living word’s judgment—then (beyond range) 4:14–16 consolation. Drift/neglect (2:1–4) if unchecked becomes Kadesh-type irreversible loss.
